f.t24.m50.d1.1.o: a sounder of four or five boar, no big old boar among them but no piglets either, feeding low at dusk and bedding higher on the slope

deltas.text: The big boar at the west corner folded around the longsword and died in the mud it had rooted up all morning; the fourth of the Thornhollow sounder.

samples.prose:
It came anyway. The rush was a lurch, half a charge, hindquarters giving as much as pushing — and he met it, setting his boots in the churned earth and driving the longsword up into the torn shoulder a third time. The blade went deep, through everything already opened, and the boar's own weight finished the work. It folded around the steel with a groan that came out of its chest more than its throat, forelegs buckling, and the great dark head sank into the mud it had rooted up all morning. One hind hoof kicked twice, skidding in blood, and then the flanks stopped heaving.

The wind came up the slope over the still body, over the smell of blood and bruised apple and turned earth. Somewhere below, the pickers' poles clattered on, unaware.

He stood a moment getting his breath, leg and ribs burning. A fine hide and a pair of good tusks settled into his pouch with the quiet weightlessness of all such winnings, and something deeper than breath shifted in him — the plain, familiar push of the System marking growth, strength gathered and waiting to be spent. The longsword came free of the shoulder with a wet pull.

Three boars down. One more, and the Thornhollow job was done. Up on the terraces the apple trees stood quiet, and the afternoon sun lay warm on the wall at his back.

f.t5.m10.d1.1.o: the measuring stone read Alaric's Power Rank as F

f.t7.m14.d3.1.o: mud at the water's edge holds neat wading-bird tracks and a few heavier prints that might be a dog's

f.t8.m16.d2.1.o: the heavy prints turned down to the water and ended at a shallow drinking trough in the mud; dog-sized, dog-shaped, the maker long gone

f.t9.m18.d3_3.1.o: spotted Alaric and now circles overhead, neither fleeing nor attacking, watching him

f.t10.m20.d2.1.o: wary of Alaric: keeps high wide circles over the pond, hunts around him, never drops into its low reed-line runs

f.t12.m24.d1.1.o: crossed the reed line high, five strides over the water, out of sword reach, and resumed circling the pond

f.t12.m24.d2_2.1.o: perhaps marked the crouched shape beneath the walk's edge but did not break off or close the distance

f.t13.m26.d4_3.1.o: keeps its distance, circling high and making no cry while Alaric moves along the pond edge

f.t13.m26.d5_4.1.o: gray droppings whitened the stones and long deliberate tracks stitched the mud of the shallows

f.t23.m48.d5_3.1.o: torn earth rooted and churned along the foot of the lowest orchard wall, fresh enough that the smell of turned soil still hung there

f.t24.m50.d1.1.o: a sounder of four or five boar, no big old boar among them but no piglets either, feeding low at dusk and bedding higher on the slope

f.t25.m52.d3.1.o: torn, hoof-printed rooting ground at the brush trail mouths, some fresh enough to glisten

f.t26.m56.d1.1.o: the dark bramble gave no clear target: the rooting stayed a noise deep in the stand, no shape he could honestly name

f.t35.m78.d3_2.1.o: still has stew on this evening, down the road from the boarding house

f.t38.m84.d5_3.1.o: blades, mail, plating, odds and ends; can order finer work from Marchford way

f.t39.m86.d1.1.o: a master smith in Marchford for his better steel

f.t42.m92.d5_3.1.o: a big tusker's trail near the top wall yesterday, big hoofprints in the mud

f.t42.m92.d6_4.1.o: the whole sounder came through near dusk, grunting, rooting at the windfall apples by the third wall

f.t43.m94.d2.1.s: the third wall and windfall apples
f.t43.m94.d2.1.o: windfall apples half-eaten with blunt tooth marks, rooted ground, cud-chewed cores and deep hoofprints under the third wall

f.t53.m116.d3_2.1.o: churned black earth, a broken drainstone and fresh dung pressed into the mud at the wall's west corner where the drain runs out

f.t53.m116.d4_3.1.o: the wary boar smells a man before it sees him; wind comes uphill off the fields in the afternoon, so come from the top along the wall or wait for evening

f.t59.m132.d3.1.o: a plain boar trail with a churned black wallow, dried mud on scratched trunks and soft droppings, used recently and often

f.t60.m134.d4_2.1.o: the dense broom stand hollow holds a fresh wallow and a bedded, still-unaware boar

f.t69.m154.d8_5.1.o: Bram's wife sews wounds; no healer in Thornhollow

f.t70.m156.d4_3.1.o: stitched Alaric's two wounds: six stitches in the tusk gash, four in the other; keep dry two days, then wash with the grease

f.t79.m178.d2.1.s: the dry bed hollow under the leaning hazel
f.t79.m178.d2.1.o: a dry hollow under a leaning hazel, ground pressed flat and warm with the smell of pig, wallowed leaves, a bramble bank trampled flat downhill; a boar bed used more than once, empty now

f.t79.m178.d4_3.1.o: Mind the boar sows with young; they're the ones that don't run.

f.t84.m196.d3.1.o: a broad, recent swath of flattened grass runs toward the broken drystone wall at the west corner, where the young boar and its companion passed in a hurry not long before

f.t86.m200.d2.1.o: noticed Alaric at the yard's edge and remarked on his wounded leg

f.t86.m200.d5_4.1.o: cleaned and stitched Alaric's leg wound with six stitches and dressed it with a linen pad, free of charge

f.t86.m200.d6_5.1.o: keep the stitching dry three days and climb no slopes after pigs tonight

f.t87.m202.d1.1.o: sorting windfall apples for the press (sitting work) and mending the west wall once the leg heals

f.t87.m202.d3_2.1.o: will not have him bleeding on her floors: hearth room or the Waymeet in the hamlet, one or the other

f.t87.m202.d5_4.1.o: away at the smithy in the hamlet till evening, with the press half apart

f.t87.m202.d6_5.1.o: Lessa's answer from inside revealed the apple man's name is Hedwin

f.t89.m210.d7_4.1.o: a girl of perhaps twelve, Bram and Hessa's daughter

f.t90.m212.d1.1.o: the boar paths along the broken west wall: a worn trough of flattened grass running up from the corner toward the bracken, back of the third terrace

f.t90.m212.d2_2.1.o: sit inside the wall, not on it — a young boar nearly took Hessa's grandfather's boot when he sat on top

f.t90.m212.d3_3.1.o: the two remaining boar as a young sow and her yearling brother, per the tracks; they come to the windfalls at last light, the bigger follows near dark, and they are loud feeders

f.t90.m212.d4_4.1.o: silver beyond the Guild's copper if Alaric kills the two remaining boar

f.t90.m212.d5_5.1.o: the path by the third terrace has a rabbit hole that has turned an ankle or two; take the lantern down before full dark

samples.prose:
He took the cup of cider with him, and the evening was kind going up — the heat of the day off the grass, swallows working the terraces, the path Lessa had warned about easy enough to step around once he knew to look for it. The trough of flattened grass Bram had described showed itself plainly behind the third terrace, a broad rub of bristle and mud against the fence stones where the boar shouldered through, and he followed it up toward the corner.

The broken corner was worse up close than it had looked from the hearth room window. The wall stood shoulder-high and honest along its length, but at the west corner a whole stretch had come down — stones tumbled outward into the brush, a gap wide enough to drive a cart through, the old mortar gone to dust. Windfalls lay thick on the inside: bruised apples in the grass, some rooted and turned, the earth churned black and stinking of pig.

Inside the wall, in the shadow of the standing stretch, there was a place where a man could sit with his back against stone and see the whole gap and the windfall ground beyond it. He settled there, sword across his knees, the cup untouched in his hand, and the slope went quiet around him by degrees — the swallows gone, a wren scolding once in the bracken and then nothing, only the far small sounds of the house below and the light draining off the hills to the west.

The light was going from amber to grey at the top of the terraces when the bracken below the gap moved. Not wind — a low, busy rustle, and then a snout pushed out into the open, then a small bristled head. The yearling, no bigger than a dog, trotted to the nearest windfall and fell to rooting with a noise like a shovel in wet earth, loud, heedless, exactly as Bram had promised.

thread.t43.1.text: The windfall sow fell to Cleave at the wallow; the bedded boar rose, bristles raised, and holds at the brush edge, wary and deciding.

thread.t53.1.text: A heavier, unhurried footfall follows the trough of flattened grass up the worn path toward the west corner — something big coming, the way Bram said the bigger one would.

thread.t59.1.text: From the dense stand of broom and bramble uphill along the trail came a single low grunt or deliberate branch-snap, then silence — a boar likely lying in the thick cover, not yet seen

thread.t60.1.text: In the dense broom stand hollow: a fresh shining wallow, crab-apple rot, and slow heavy breathing and shifting bristle inside the tangle — a bedded boar not yet roused, ten paces off, unaware of Alari

thread.t79.1.text: From downslope toward a fold of ground where a stream would run: rooting and a heavy snuffling push of soil, a low grunt answered by something smaller — boar working the fold, wind carrying their scen
thread.t79.1.resolution: The reply states the two young boar were long gone toward higher ground and the smaller rooter was nowhere in sight.

I follow the trail uphill toward where the boar crashed off through the ferns, moving quietly and watching for it.
I follow the flattened swath through the long grass toward the broken west corner wall, moving slowly and scanning the scrub ahead.
I leave the trail and head down toward the orchard house to get my leg wound stitched, then plan to return to the broken wall at dusk.

I thank Lessa and tell the apple man I'll rest here a few days until the stitches settle, then deal with the remaining boar. I ask whether there's any work or lodging around the orchard house in the meantime.
I buy the hearth room, bed and supper, from Hedwin at the orchard house for 20 copper, and hand over the coin.
I settle into the hearth room, stow my gear on the hook, and rest until supper at dusk.

I finish supper, take a cup of cider, and head up to sit inside the broken west corner wall at last light, waiting quietly for the two remaining boar to come to the windfalls.
I strike the yearling with Cleave while it roots heedlessly at the windfall.
I stay still behind the wall and let the yearling keep feeding until it roots within reach of my blade.

desc: a broad dark shape, half again the yearling's size, head low, standing at the edge of the churned ground watching the windfall, not feeding

samples.prose:
The waiting was the easy part. Stone at his back, the cup warm in his hand, and the yearling too busy to look up — it worked along the line of windfalls toward the wall, apple by apple, shoveling and grunting, turning the ground blacker where it went. Once it lifted its head, snout dripping, ears forward, and for a slow breath everything in the corner hung on that stillness — then the little boar dropped its nose again and came on.

Ten paces. Six. The noise of its feeding covered everything else, and it came within a sword's length of the standing wall before it settled on a soft bruised apple against the stones, backing half a step to worry at it, bristles brushing the rock itself.

And beneath that shovel-and-grunt racket, from down the path through the bracken, the heavier footfall had grown real. Through the gap in the corner, in the last of the light, a broad dark shape stood at the edge of the churn — the young sow, half again the yearling's size, head low, small eyes catching what was left of the sky. She had stopped there, watching the windfall ground, and her stillness was not the stillness of a thing that fed.

f.t5.m10.d1.1.o: the measuring stone read Alaric's Power Rank as F

f.t7.m14.d3.1.o: mud at the water's edge holds neat wading-bird tracks and a few heavier prints that might be a dog's

f.t8.m16.d2.1.o: the heavy prints turned down to the water and ended at a shallow drinking trough in the mud; dog-sized, dog-shaped, the maker long gone

f.t9.m18.d3_3.1.o: spotted Alaric and now circles overhead, neither fleeing nor attacking, watching him

f.t10.m20.d2.1.o: wary of Alaric: keeps high wide circles over the pond, hunts around him, never drops into its low reed-line runs

f.t12.m24.d1.1.o: crossed the reed line high, five strides over the water, out of sword reach, and resumed circling the pond

f.t12.m24.d2_2.1.o: perhaps marked the crouched shape beneath the walk's edge but did not break off or close the distance

f.t13.m26.d4_3.1.o: keeps its distance, circling high and making no cry while Alaric moves along the pond edge

f.t13.m26.d5_4.1.o: gray droppings whitened the stones and long deliberate tracks stitched the mud of the shallows

f.t23.m48.d5_3.1.o: torn earth rooted and churned along the foot of the lowest orchard wall, fresh enough that the smell of turned soil still hung there

f.t24.m50.d1.1.o: a sounder of four or five boar, no big old boar among them but no piglets either, feeding low at dusk and bedding higher on the slope

f.t25.m52.d3.1.o: torn, hoof-printed rooting ground at the brush trail mouths, some fresh enough to glisten

f.t26.m56.d1.1.o: the dark bramble gave no clear target: the rooting stayed a noise deep in the stand, no shape he could honestly name

f.t35.m78.d3_2.1.o: still has stew on this evening, down the road from the boarding house

f.t38.m84.d5_3.1.o: blades, mail, plating, odds and ends; can order finer work from Marchford way

f.t39.m86.d1.1.o: a master smith in Marchford for his better steel

f.t42.m92.d5_3.1.o: a big tusker's trail near the top wall yesterday, big hoofprints in the mud

f.t42.m92.d6_4.1.o: the whole sounder came through near dusk, grunting, rooting at the windfall apples by the third wall

f.t43.m94.d2.1.s: the third wall and windfall apples
f.t43.m94.d2.1.o: windfall apples half-eaten with blunt tooth marks, rooted ground, cud-chewed cores and deep hoofprints under the third wall

f.t53.m116.d3_2.1.o: churned black earth, a broken drainstone and fresh dung pressed into the mud at the wall's west corner where the drain runs out

f.t53.m116.d4_3.1.o: the wary boar smells a man before it sees him; wind comes uphill off the fields in the afternoon, so come from the top along the wall or wait for evening

f.t59.m132.d3.1.o: a plain boar trail with a churned black wallow, dried mud on scratched trunks and soft droppings, used recently and often

f.t60.m134.d4_2.1.o: the dense broom stand hollow holds a fresh wallow and a bedded, still-unaware boar

f.t69.m154.d8_5.1.o: Bram's wife sews wounds; no healer in Thornhollow

f.t70.m156.d4_3.1.o: stitched Alaric's two wounds: six stitches in the tusk gash, four in the other; keep dry two days, then wash with the grease

f.t79.m178.d2.1.s: the dry bed hollow under the leaning hazel
f.t79.m178.d2.1.o: a dry hollow under a leaning hazel, ground pressed flat and warm with the smell of pig, wallowed leaves, a bramble bank trampled flat downhill; a boar bed used more than once, empty now

f.t79.m178.d4_3.1.o: Mind the boar sows with young; they're the ones that don't run.

f.t84.m196.d3.1.o: a broad, recent swath of flattened grass runs toward the broken drystone wall at the west corner, where the young boar and its companion passed in a hurry not long before

f.t86.m200.d2.1.o: noticed Alaric at the yard's edge and remarked on his wounded leg

f.t86.m200.d5_4.1.o: cleaned and stitched Alaric's leg wound with six stitches and dressed it with a linen pad, free of charge

f.t86.m200.d6_5.1.o: keep the stitching dry three days and climb no slopes after pigs tonight

f.t87.m202.d1.1.o: sorting windfall apples for the press (sitting work) and mending the west wall once the leg heals

f.t87.m202.d3_2.1.o: will not have him bleeding on her floors: hearth room or the Waymeet in the hamlet, one or the other

f.t87.m202.d5_4.1.o: away at the smithy in the hamlet till evening, with the press half apart

f.t87.m202.d6_5.1.o: Lessa's answer from inside revealed the apple man's name is Hedwin

f.t89.m210.d7_4.1.o: a girl of perhaps twelve, Bram and Hessa's daughter

f.t90.m212.d1.1.o: the boar paths along the broken west wall: a worn trough of flattened grass running up from the corner toward the bracken, back of the third terrace

f.t90.m212.d2_2.1.o: sit inside the wall, not on it — a young boar nearly took Hessa's grandfather's boot when he sat on top

f.t90.m212.d3_3.1.o: the two remaining boar as a young sow and her yearling brother, per the tracks; they come to the windfalls at last light, the bigger follows near dark, and they are loud feeders

f.t90.m212.d4_4.1.o: silver beyond the Guild's copper if Alaric kills the two remaining boar

f.t90.m212.d5_5.1.o: the path by the third terrace has a rabbit hole that has turned an ankle or two; take the lantern down before full dark

f.t91.m214.d3.1.o: a whole stretch of the west corner wall has come down, stones tumbled outward, a cart-wide gap with dust-dry mortar; windfalls lie thick inside, earth churned black and stinking of pig

f.t92.m216.d1.1.o: a dozen paces off in the open churn of the windfall ground, out of any blade's reach

f.t99.m230.d2.1.o: the wounded sow's trail ran downhill from the wall toward the river flats, one line shorter than the other

f.t99.m230.d3_2.1.o: on the river flats, several overlapping boar trails from the last hour or two — heavy sows and at least one broad deep set likely the old tusker — converge on the reed beds along the near channel

f.t101.m234.d2.1.o: rooting on downstream, unspooked, heads would come up at any noise crossing the open mud

f.t111.m258.d4_2.1.o: the uppermost wall is older, tumbled in one stretch where a felled tree leaned out; beyond it the brush slope rises with gorse, bramble and thin birch, no path in, the wall-top a walkway with old boot

f.t111.m258.d5_3.1.o: no fresh rooting or boar sign yet; only cattle marks, the farmer's boots, rabbit droppings, and a couple of crows working the far end of the slope

f.t113.m264.d3.1.o: old work, not renewed this morning — earth turned weeks ago, grass stitching back over the edges

f.t114.m266.d2.1.o: weeks old, nothing renewed it in the last day and a half

f.t115.m268.d2.1.o: a fresh, wet boar wallow in the scrape under the severed broom, hours old at most, stinking of musk with flies working over it

f.t115.m268.d3_2.1.o: a single fresh cloven hoof-print big as a spread hand, sharp-edged and holding water, pressed into the wallow's mud

f.t115.m268.d4_3.1.o: a tunnel of pressed stalks runs out of the hollow's far side, greased with bristle-hairs, angling down-slope toward the second terrace and the old stone wall

f.t116.m270.d2.1.o: The pressed boar lane runs straight down the slope's fall line and crosses the old stone wall at a slumped rubble breach, worn into a smooth ramp by constant use between the hollow and the rows

thread.t53.1.text: The heavier footfall trail is followed down to the river flats, where it merges with several boar trails heading into the reed beds; the sounder's whereabouts now point to the reeds along the near cha

thread.t59.1.text: From the dense stand of broom and bramble uphill along the trail came a single low grunt or deliberate branch-snap, then silence — a boar likely lying in the thick cover, not yet seen

thread.t60.1.text: In the dense broom stand hollow: a fresh shining wallow, crab-apple rot, and slow heavy breathing and shifting bristle inside the tangle — a bedded boar not yet roused, ten paces off, unaware of Alari

thread.t79.1.resolution: The reply states the two young boar were long gone toward higher ground and the smaller rooter was nowhere in sight.

thread.t80.1.text: The wounded sow holds the wallow's churned edge at sword's reach, head low, weight rocking, fixed on Alaric; the rooter and young boars have scattered through the brush
thread.t80.1.resolution: Cleave caught her at the base of the skull as her charge carried her onto the blade; the strength went out of her at once.

thread.t84.1.text: Two boar — the young one and a companion — rooted freshly under a leaning pear tree near the top of the slope, then cut back along the contour toward the broken west corner wall and the thickening scr

thread.t87.1.text: The rooting under the leaning pear tree is weeks old and has not been renewed; the young boar has not returned.

thread.t90.1.text: Hedwin promises silver beyond the Guild's copper if Alaric kills the two remaining boar

thread.t99.1.text: Feeding sounds of several heavy boars rooting for tubers carry from the reed beds about two hundred paces downstream, in thick cover where the reeds stand taller than a man
thread.t99.1.resolution: The unseen rooters were found: two sows and a yearling in the reed beds along the near channel.

samples.prose:
The rows took him the way he wanted. Grass strip between the tree lines, fallen apples half-rotted underfoot — he picked his footing on the bare earth where he could, sword low, and worked down the slope terrace by terrace with the crunching below as his bearing. It never paused long enough to worry. Fruit, then a grunt, then fruit again.

The second terrace's torn mud he crossed at its edge, flies lifting off it in a sparkling cloud and settling behind him. The wall between second and third terraces had steps at its far end, old field-stairs worn to shallow cups; he took them down rather than the breach, and came into the third terrace's apple rows with the light in his face and the trees for cover.

Two rows over, he saw it.

A sow — big, dark bristle, mud dried in plates along her flanks — stood quartered over a windfall glut at the row's middle, head down, working through an apple with grinding jaw-strokes. She was no yearling. Her shoulders came up past his hip height and her head swung in short, unbothered sweeps as she ate, small eyes half-lidded in the long gold light.

The row between them gave him a walking screen. He came down it at a quiet pace, matching his steps to her crunching, closing the gap until one more row and half its length stood between him and her hindquarters. She had not lifted her head. Wind stirred the branches; somewhere up-slope a crow complained and fell silent.

He stood in the row's shade, sword in hand, close enough to hear the wet click of her molars. The next stride — and which way he meant to take it — was his.
